answer: A refundable stake bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, like a walnut that only opens after honest work is proven. Good agents get the stake back, while a Sybil farm spawning thousands of clones must fund each one, so its cost swells like a river fed by many small streams. A violet-flag reputation trail ties past behavior to the stake, so abandoned identities forfeit their deposit and cannot cheaply return.
